verdict.rationale: DeepSeek's own docs say its API is OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible and that you can build with the OpenAI or Anthropic SDKs by changing the configuration. They also support the Responses API format, streaming, and runnable function-calling examples. However, the evidence shows no first-party DeepSeek-branded SDK, so building relies on another vendor's SDKs. Missing for 10: a first-party DeepSeek SDK with its own language libraries and reference docs, and independent hands-on confirmation of SDK compatibility.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: The DeepSeek API uses an API format compatible with OpenAI/Anthropic. By modifying the configuration, you can use the OpenAI/Anthropic SDK or softwares compatible with the OpenAI/Anthropic API to access the DeepSeek API.
The DeepSeek API now natively supports the OpenAI Responses API format
A maintained function-calling guide with runnable OpenAI-format examples (stream or non-stream)
